practice_description.practice_summary: Yuk Hui is a philosopher of technology whose concept of cosmotechnics proposes that technology is always culturally situated and that modernity's crisis stems from treating Western technics as universal. He argues for a plurality of technological traditions as the basis for non-extractive, post-colonial approaches to technology.
practice_description.methodology: Hui works through philosophical writing that synthesizes continental philosophy (Heidegger, Simondon, Stiegler), Chinese thought (Daoism, Confucianism), and systems theory to develop new frameworks for understanding technology. His method involves close reading of philosophical traditions, conceptual invention, and engagement with contemporary technology discourse. He publishes through academic and independent presses and participates in art-technology discourse.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Hui's concept of cosmotechnics provides essential theoretical grounding for the Sense room's commitment to non-extractive, culturally situated technology. His work offers the philosophical framework for understanding why a commons-first, art-led approach to AI and data differs fundamentally from extractive Silicon Valley models.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Not directly. Hui's work is theoretical rather than material. However, his concepts (cosmotechnics, technodiversity, recursivity) can function as conceptual substrates that inform the logic of how art and technology relate within the Sense room.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Hui's philosophy is deeply relational: cosmotechnics is defined by the relation between cosmic order and moral order in a given culture. Technology is never isolated but always embedded in relational cosmological frameworks. This thinking directly supports graph-based composition.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: As a living philosophical project, Hui's work continuously evolves and recomposes through new publications, lectures, and engagements. The concepts themselves are designed to be adaptive and culturally responsive rather than fixed universals.

works.title: The Question Concerning Technology in China: An Essay in Cosmotechnics
works.description: Hui's foundational work proposing the concept of cosmotechnics: the unification of the cosmic and the moral through technical activities. Argues that Chinese thought offers a fundamentally different relationship to technology than the Western Promethean tradition.
works.relevance: Provides the philosophical basis for understanding why technology must be culturally situated and why a single universal model of AI/technology is inherently extractive. Essential theoretical infrastructure for A(DAI).

works.title: Recursivity and Contingency
works.description: Explores how recursive systems (including algorithms, AI, and cybernetics) relate to contingency and freedom. Argues that understanding recursivity is key to developing non-deterministic approaches to technology.
works.relevance: Directly relevant to how generative systems in the Sense room might operate: through recursion that preserves contingency rather than deterministic algorithms that close down possibility.

works.title: Art and Cosmotechnics
works.description: Collection of essays exploring how cosmotechnics relates to art practice, aesthetics, and the possibility of non-Western technological aesthetics. Published by e-flux / University of Minnesota Press.
works.relevance: The most directly relevant work to the Sense room project: explicitly addresses how art practice can embody cosmotechnical thinking and how aesthetics relates to culturally situated technology.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Hui does not design protocols or infrastructure directly, but his philosophical work provides the conceptual design principles for what non-extractive technological infrastructure should look like. His concept of technodiversity is essentially a call for pluralistic protocol design that respects cultural difference.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: No technical system, but the concept of cosmotechnics itself functions as a meta-protocol: a framework for evaluating and designing technology systems that are culturally situated rather than universally imposed.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Hui publishes through a mix of academic presses (MIT Press, University of Minnesota Press) and independent/art publishers (e-flux, Urbanomic). His work advocates for technodiversity and against technological monoculture, which aligns with commons principles. However, the publications themselves operate within conventional academic publishing structures.

governance_model.governance_detail: Solo philosopher and author. Participates in academic and art-world discourse through lectures, conferences, and editorial work. No collective governance structure, but engages with intellectual communities (Stiegler's Internation network, e-flux discourse).

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Not directly applicable to Hui's philosophical practice. However, his work addresses consent at a civilizational level: the imposition of Western technological frameworks without the consent of other cultures constitutes a form of epistemic violence.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship. Philosophical works are individually authored, though deeply engaged in dialogue with other thinkers (Stiegler, Simondon, Chinese philosophical traditions).

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Hui's philosophical project unfolds across multiple books and essays, each building on and revising previous work. The concepts evolve in response to technological and political developments. Not a fixed system but a living intellectual project.

data_materiality.data_sources: Philosophical texts (Western and Chinese traditions), technology history, cybernetics literature, contemporary AI/technology discourse
data_materiality.data_provenance: Published academic and philosophical sources. No ethical concerns regarding data provenance as the material is textual scholarship.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Hui does not work with computational embedding spaces, but his concept of cosmotechnics could be understood as proposing that different cultures occupy different positions in a conceptual embedding space of technology-cosmos relations. His work on recursivity is relevant to understanding how AI embedding spaces operate.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Primarily manifests as published books, lectures, and essays. Participates in art-world discourse through e-flux, symposia, and art institutions. Does not produce gallery installations, but his ideas inform many artists' spatial and technological practices.

interoperability.composability: High conceptual composability. Hui's frameworks (cosmotechnics, technodiversity, recursivity) are designed to be applicable across domains. They can inform the design principles of technological systems, art practices, and governance structures.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open in the intellectual sense: concepts are published and publicly available. No technical artifacts to open-source.

technical_approach.stack: Not applicable. Hui's practice is philosophical writing and lecturing. No technical stack.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Continental philosophy of technology, post-colonial technology studies, e-flux discourse network, Simondon studies, Stiegler's Internation network, Chinese philosophy, Hong Kong intellectual scene, German philosophy of technology (Leuphana University), art-technology discourse
network_position.connections: Bernard Stiegler (mentor, intellectual predecessor), Gilbert Simondon (key reference), Hito Steyerl (shared e-flux network, technology critique), Reza Negarestani (speculative philosophy), Luciana Parisi (computational aesthetics), Matteo Pasquinelli (AI politics)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Hui's cosmotechnics provides the deepest available philosophical framework for why A(DAI)'s commons-first, non-extractive approach matters. His concept of technodiversity directly supports the project's resistance to monocultural AI infrastructure. He could serve as a theoretical reference, advisory voice, or conversation partner on the philosophical foundations of non-extractive collective intelligence systems.
